subject: Dedicated capacity ramp schedule — multi-year prepay negotiation with ArgoML
messages:
From: Samantha Hughes <samantha.hughes@argoml.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated ramp schedule — initial ask

Hey David,

Thanks again for taking the time last week. We’re putting together an internal recommendation for a Dedicated commitment with Redwood and want to validate a few items before we engage procurement. High-level ask below: 

- Target contract: 3 year prepay (annual invoicing preferred)
- Capacity profile we are modeling: Year 1 = ~30% of final peak GPU pool, Year 2 = ~40%, Year 3 = ~30% (phased onboarding to match product rollout)
- Primary concern: front-loaded performance for Q1–Q2 of Year 1 to support initial inference volume spikes; we’d like the ability to move capacity faster if needed
- Seeking a discount ladder tied to annual prepay amount + multi-year commit (please show baseline, 2-year, 3-year pricing and an escalation credit if we frontload year 1)
- Need clarity on TPM vs GPU billing parity and whether TPU-like workloads can be accommodated on the Dedicated pool

Can you and your team sketch a term sheet that covers: ramp schedule options (phased delivery and true-up mechanics), invoice cadence (annual vs front-loaded), early-ramp credits, and cancellation/true-up protections? Also attaching a short SOW outline for context.

Procurement will expect SOC2 + network isolation notes, but we can handle that later — for now a commercial term sheet is our priority.

Appreciate it,

Samantha Hughes
Head of Cloud Ops, ArgoML
[sent from mobile]

Attachments: ArgoML-SOW-outline.docx

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Hughes <samantha.hughes@argoml.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 10:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated ramp schedule — initial ask

Samantha —

Thanks for the clear brief and the SOW outline. I’ve looped in Lauren (Revenue Ops) and Ben (Solutions) to make sure we cover billing amortization and the runbook for phased provisioning. High-level counterproposal below; I’m attaching a compact proposal PDF for your procurement team to review.

Key commercial options we recommend:

1) Staggered Onramp (balanced smoothing)
   - Year 1: 35% delivered at contract start, Year 2: 40%, Year 3: 25%
   - True-up window: quarterly true-ups with a 90-day lookback to handle spikes

2) Frontload Option (accelerated capacity)
   - If ArgoML frontloads >=45% in Year 1 prepay, we will apply a +6% one-time prepay uplift on top of standard multi-year discount (applies to Year 1 invoice only)
   - This is paired with a carryover credit: unused Year 1 capacity can be rolled into Year 2 as credit for 12 months

3) Discount ladder (examples)
   - 1-year baseline: list - 0%
   - 2-year commit: -8%
   - 3-year commit: -12%
   - Frontload uplift (Year1 >=45%): additional -6% on Year1 invoice (as above)

4) TPM/GPU parity & spikes
   - We support TPU-style workloads on select GPU SKUs; we’ll include a TPM equivalency table and a spike cushion (burst capacity) option in the full term sheet. Pricing for TPU-equivalent usage will be quoted as a per-TPM equivalent rate if sustained beyond burst windows.

5) Billing & protections
   - Preferred: annual invoicing with milestone-based delivery schedule (invoices issued at contract signature + annual anniversaries)
   - Cancellation & scale-down: 30–60 day notice windows with true-up/credit mechanics; we can structure an escrowed credit if ArgoML requires additional cancellation protection

Next steps:
- I’ll send a concise redwood_dedicated_proposal_v1.pdf to procurement with the firm pricing bands and an amortization example.
- Can we schedule a 45-min working session this week (ops + procurement + solutions) to align on which ramp option you prefer and procurement timing?

If you think procurement will insist on a larger Year1 frontload to lock capacity, call that out in the meeting and we’ll price a second option (frontload-first).

Thanks,

—David
David Kim
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_proposal_v1.pdf

From: Samantha Hughes <samantha.hughes@argoml.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: ArgoML Procurement <procurement@argoml.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2026 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated ramp schedule — initial ask

On Mon, Jun 15, 2026 at 10:24 AM David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com> wrote:
> Samantha —
> 
> Thanks for the clear brief and the SOW outline. I’ve looped in Lauren (Revenue Ops) and Ben (Solutions) to make sure we cover billing amortization and the runbook for phased provisioning. High-level counterproposal below; I’m attaching a compact proposal PDF for your procurement team to review.
>
> [proposal summary snipped]

David — thanks for the quick turnaround and the options. A couple of clarifications from procurement and platform: 

- Procurement note: our standard internal policy would prefer Year 1 >=50% if feasible; it secures capacity and shortens the onboarding runway for the teams. If Redwood can give an additional commercial sweetener for Year1 >=50% (e.g., price uplift or additional credits) that would be compelling.
- Platform note: we will have TPM-heavy inference bursts as we ramp experimental features — want to confirm the spike cushion details and how billable TPM equivalents are calculated for burst vs sustained usage.
- Timeline: procurement aims to finish commercial review by the end of next week if we can get a single consolidated term sheet and an estimated invoice schedule.

We’ve cc’d procurement here. Our procurement lead (procurement@argoml.com) will attach a short procurement checklist; I’ve also attached their initial note for your reference.

Can you run the frontload scenario (Year1 = 50% prepay) with: 1) an explicit uplift or credit line we can show to execs, 2) amortized invoice schedule across the three years, and 3) clearly called out spike/TPM parity language?

Appreciate it — will set up the cross-functional call once we have your updated sheet.

Sam
Samantha Hughes
Head of Cloud Ops, ArgoML

Attachments: procurement-note.pdf

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Hughes <samantha.hughes@argoml.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated ramp schedule — frontload scenario and next steps

Sam —

Appreciate the clarity. We ran the ledger with Finance and put together an updated commercial that addresses the Year1 frontload. High level summary below and I’ve attached a clean PDF and SOW draft for procurement/legal review.

Summary: Frontload (Year1 = 50%) scenario-
- Pricing: base 3-year commit = -12% off list. Frontload premium: additional -6% applied to Year1 invoice if Year1 prepaid >=50%. Net effect: Year1 effective discount = -18% vs list for Year1 invoice only. Years 2–3 remain at the 3-year commit discount (no extra uplift).
- Carryover credits: unused Year1 prepaid capacity can be carried into Year2 as a credit at the effective rate paid for 12 months; credits cannot be refunded but can be applied to future usage or to increase Year2 provisioning without re-pricing.
- Spike/TPM handling: we will provide a TPM equivalency table and two buckets:
   a) Burst cushion: short-term free burst up to 10% of provisioned capacity per quarter (non-billable, designed for experimental spikes)
   b) Sustained TPM usage: billed by TPM-equivalent rate when sustained beyond 7 days or when average daily TPM exceeds the cushion threshold; referenced table included in SOW addendum.
- Invoice schedule: Signature (Year1 invoice) due at contract signing. Year2 and Year3 invoices due on each contract anniversary. We include an amortization schedule in the attached proposal so your finance team can model capex/opex impacts.
- Protections: 45-day contract scale-down notice with quarterly true-up; we can add an escrow mechanic if procurement requests additional cancellation protection (we’ve priced escrow as a % of Year1 prepay if needed).

Next steps:
1) Review attached redwood_dedicated_proposal_v2.pdf + SOW-draft.docx (procurement & legal)
2) If acceptable, I’ll generate a DocuSign envelope with the chosen ramp option and milestone invoice details for signature.
3) Schedule a 45-min cross-functional call to confirm operations runbook (solutions + platform + your Cloud Ops).

If procurement confirms Year1 >=50% today we can hold capacity for 10 business days while the legal team finalizes contract language. Let me know if you want a brief call to walk through the amortization example.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this over the finish line.

—David
David Kim
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0129
